unit.title: What agents are, and when to trust them

lesson.title: What its tools allow
lesson.subtitle: An agent acts only through its tools

video.title: What its tools allow
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds, one recurring teacher character. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Mr Okafor — science teacher, Nigeria (main character)
Mr Joseph Mwangi — computer studies teacher, Kenya (cameo)
Ms Salma Haddad — secondary maths teacher (cameo)
Narrator — the Darsi voice (warm, peer to peer)

chapters.label: A list of tools, and their details
Four ways a request can go

scenes.visual: A list: “I can’t”; No booking tool.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: I asked our school agent to book the bus for the science trip. It said it couldn’t. I was annoyed at first. Then I realised: it had no tool for booking!

scenes.animation: The Darsi mark pops in; the title slides up.
scenes.narration: Today: what an agent’s tools allow, and what a good agent does when they don’t.

scenes.visual: A list: Your request; The tools that are on; It acts only through its tools; No tool, no job.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: It reads a list of tools
scenes.narration: Before it acts, the model reads your request and the list of tools that are switched on. Darsi Tiny has ten, from a calculator to reminders and messages. It acts only through those tools, so no tool means no job.

scenes.visual: Code typed out on a card: timetable{"class":"6B", …
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Each tool needs details. The weather tool needs a place and a day. The timetable needs a class and a day. The model copies those details from your words into the call.

scenes.visual: A list: Uses a tool; Says the tool is off; Says “I can’t”; Asks for a missing detail.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: Four ways a request can go
scenes.narration: So a request can go four ways. It uses a tool. It says the tool it needs is off. It says it can’t, because no tool fits. Or it asks for a missing detail.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: I switched the weather tool off and asked about Kafi: it said the tool is off, instead of guessing. Then I asked it to book a bus ticket. No tool can, so it said so.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: What if you leave out a detail? Ask what the weather is tomorrow, and Darsi Tiny asks back: which village? Reply Dala, and it calls the weather tool. Asking beats guessing.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: The tool is off: now what?
scenes.narration: Quick check! The reminder tool is switched off, and you ask for a reminder. What should a good agent do?

scenes.visual: A list: Say so plainly; Never pretend it worked; Then you do it yourself.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Say the tool is off. An agent that pretends hides what really happened. Being told no is useful: you know to do it yourself.

scenes.visual: A list: Class 9Z becomes 9C; France goes to the glossary; Check every call.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: But it doesn’t always know its limits. Ask what class 9Z has tomorrow, a class that doesn’t exist, and it calls the timetable for 9C. Ask what is the capital of France, and it tries the glossary. So check every call.

scenes.visual: A list: Ask about Kafi; Switch a tool off, ask again; Leave out a detail; Class 9Z: read the check.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: App lab: how an agent picks a tool
scenes.narration: In the app, ask about the weather in Kafi, then switch the weather tool off and ask again. Ask for something no tool can do, and leave out a detail. Then try class 9Z, and read the check under the call.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Your turn. I asked what the weather is tomorrow, and the agent asked me: which village? Why?

scenes.visual: Summary points: Only the tools that are on; Details from your words; It says so, or asks.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: Only the tools that are on · Details from your words · It says so, or asks
scenes.narration: It needs a place. Remember: an agent acts only through the tools that are on, and fills in details from your words. A good agent says when it can’t, or asks, instead of guessing.

scenes.visual: A list: Six tool cards per group; Read out a request; A tool, a question, or “I can’t”?; Turn a card over, play again.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Try it in class tomorrow: play The toolbox. Groups get six tool cards, and you read out requests. For each, they decide: use a tool, ask for a detail, or say I can’t. Then turn a card over and play again.

checkpoints.prompt: The reminder tool is switched off, and you ask for a reminder. What should a good agent do?

options.text: Find another way to set it
Say that the reminder tool is off
Say it’s done, to keep you happy

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — saying the tool is off tells you the truth, so you know to set the reminder yourself.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — finding a way round, or pretending, hides what really happened. A good agent says the tool is off.

checkpoints.prompt: You ask “What’s the weather tomorrow?” and the agent replies “Which village?”. Why?

options.text: The weather tool needs a place, and you gave none
It has never heard of any village

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — a detail the tool needs was missing, so it asked instead of guessing.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — it isn’t broken. The weather tool needs a place and a day, and your request had no place.
